title: 91學年度指定科目考試英文考科

sections.title: 一、詞彙與慣用語(15%)
sections.instructions: 說明：第1至15題，每題選出最適當的一個選項，標示在答案卡之「選擇題答案區」。每題答對得1分，答錯倒扣1/3分。未答者，不給分亦不扣分。

questions.stem: With her teachers’ and parents’ ______, Jane regained her confidence and has made great progress.
One of Jane’s finest qualities is that she takes the ______. She always takes the necessary action and does not wait for orders.
Mr. Li is a senior ______ at a local bank. He keeps and examines financial records of people and companies.
Jack doesn’t look ______, but he is, in fact, excellent at sports, especially baseball.
The jury spent over five hours trying to decide whether the defendant is ______ or guilty.
Now that my computer is connected to the Internet, I can browse e-papers, send and receive e-mail, and ______ software.
The traffic on Main Street was ______ for several hours due to a car accident in which six people were injured.
Hundreds of people ______ in the desert storm and many more were left homeless.
Mike arrived at the meeting ______ at ten o’clock—as it was scheduled—not a minute early or late.
A power failure ______ darkened the whole city, and it was not until two hours later that electricity was restored.
Sam couldn’t ______ how to print out the document until the teacher showed it to him.
When they go for a walk, Johnny has to take long steps to ______ with his father.
The man is ______ a serious nervous breakdown because he is unable to deal with pressure from daily life.
______ treating the homeless man as a shame of the society, Mrs. Wang provided him with food and water.
Mrs. Lin ______ her husband’s complaints because, to her, facing the music is more constructive than complaining all day.

sections.title: 二、綜合測驗(15%)
sections.instructions: 說明：第16至30題，每題一個空格。請依文意選出最適當的一個選項，標示在答案卡之「選擇題答案區」。每題答對得1分，答錯倒扣1/3分。未答者，不給分亦不扣分。

groups.passage: More than 2.7 billion people will face severe shortages of fresh water by 2025. There is, [[16]], only a limited amount of water on the planet. Less than 3 percent of the world’s water is fresh, and most of [[17]] is trapped in polar ice or buried underground in springs too deep to reach. Freshwater lakes, rivers and reservoirs may seem [[18]] but provide just a drop in the bucket. Even [[19]] supplies are sufficient or plentiful, they are increasingly at risk due to various forms of pollution. Fierce national competition [[20]] water resources has prompted fears that water issues contain the seeds of violent conflict. International cooperation is therefore by all means urgent.

tags.key_phrase: most of it (= the world’s fresh water)
may seem numerous but provide just a drop in the bucket

tags.topic: global freshwater shortage and the risk of conflict over water

groups.passage: There are six international science Olympiads in the world. They are all organized with a simple intention—to [[21]] global understanding and mutual appreciation among young scientists in all countries. Each of the six science Olympiads [[22]] its specific aims. The aims of the International Mathematical Olympiad (IMO), for example, are three-fold. With arduous but interesting math problems, the first aim of the IMO is to discover, to encourage and, most important of all, to challenge [[23]] gifted young people all over the world. Secondly, it is by participating in any IMO contest that young mathematicians of all countries can foster friendly [[24]]. Based upon its second aim, more international exchanges are encouraged and established. Any IMO contest brings not only young mathematicians together but also their instructors; [[25]], the IMO has its final aim to create opportunities for the exchange of information on math schedules and practice throughout the world.

tags.key_phrase: Each of the + 複數名詞 + 單數動詞

tags.topic: the aims of the international science Olympiads (IMO)

groups.passage: Many entertainment celebrities, on April 5, 2002, attended an anti-piracy demonstration in Taipei. The purpose of the rally was to ask fans to respect the copyright and to stop buying [[26]] CDs. Although the intellectual property right is to be protected by law, the fans may think otherwise. Obviously, it is the recording industry that wants to [[27]] piracy. Celebrities in the rally probably have no idea about how much a CD of their music albums costs. After signing million-dollar contracts with recording companies, singers devote most of their time [[28]] their music perfect while companies are busy commercializing their products. It is the fans that support the kingdoms of the recording companies; [[29]], the industry never gives its feedback to the fans—by lowering the prices of CDs. It is an easy arithmetic [[30]]. When one can buy a CD of pop music for NT$50 anywhere on the streets, why does he or she want to spend NT$300 or more for the same one?

tags.topic: an anti-piracy rally in Taipei and the high prices of music CDs

sections.title: 三、文意選填(10%)
sections.instructions: 說明：第31至40題，每題一個空格。請依文意在文章後所提供的 (A) 到 (J) 選項中分別選出最適當者，並將其字母代號標示在答案卡之「選擇題答案區」。每題答對得1分，答錯倒扣1/9分。未答者，不給分亦不扣分。

groups.passage:
Are you someone who practically lives in front of the computer—a mouse potato? Or are you nervous about new technology—a technophobe? [[31]], if you want to master the English language, you will need to be [[32]] those new computer words that seem to be popping up everywhere.
Luckily, most computer words are easy to learn. [[33]], many of these words probably already have similar forms in your own language. [[34]], the German word for computer is Computer, in South American Spanish it is computador, and in Japanese we [[35]] konpyuta.
Another reason why computer words are easy to learn is that many of them are so[[36]]. They are words that often make us smile when we first hear them such as [[37]] (traditional mail rather than Internet-based mail) or wysiwyg (what-you-see-is-what-you-get).
To get a feeling for computer words, it helps to [[38]] the world that created them— cyberculture, as it is often called. The computer industry is [[39]] young people who think of themselves as very different from [[40]] business people in suits. It is a world that avoids heavy scientific-sounding language in favor of words that are simple, fresh and playful.

tags.topic: why English computer words are easy to learn (cyberculture vocabulary)

sections.title: 四、篇章結構(10%)
sections.instructions: 說明：第41至50題，每題一個空格。請依文意在文章後所提供的 (A) 到 (E) 選項中分別選出最適當者，填入空格中，使篇章結構清晰有條理，並將其英文字母代號標示在答案卡之「選擇題答案區」。每題答對得1分，答錯倒扣1/4分。未答者，不給分亦不扣分。

groups.passage:
Fiction is the name we use for stories that are make-believe, such as Harry Potter or Alice in the Wonderland. [[41]] It can be so close to the truth that it seems as real as something that happened to you this morning. Or, fiction can be as fantastic as the most unbelievable fairy tale.
Not everything in a fictional story has to be made up. [[42]] You, of course, are real, and the moon is real, and many of the things that you could describe, such as the stars, the wind, and the pull of gravity, would be real. [[43]] It would be a trip you took in your imagination.
Nonfiction, on the other hand, is all about true things. [[44]] Someone’s biography is nonfiction; so is your autobiography. So are articles in your local newspaper, and school reports on science. [[45]] Imagine writing history about the 1989 San Francisco earthquake, or a report about a high school sports team. An old proverb says, “Truth is stranger than fiction.” Do you think that’s true?

options_bank.C: But your trip through space would be fiction.
options_bank.D: You could write a story in which you fly to the moon.
options_bank.E: But fiction isn’t always different from the way things usually are.

tags.topic: the difference between fiction and nonfiction

groups.passage: Windshield wipers of a car were invented by Mary Anderson on a trip in New York City in 1903. While touring the city on a streetcar, Mary was not interested in the views on the streets. [[46]] Repeatedly, the motorman had to get out of the streetcar to wipe off the snow and ice collected on the windshield. New York streetcar motormen at that time had tried various ways to solve this problem. [[47]] Mary, sitting on her seat, quickly drew her device in her sketchbook. [[48]] Mary’s device allowed the motorman to use a lever inside the streetcar to activate a swinging arm on the windshield to wipe off the snow and ice. Because the device was first designed for cold weather, it could be easily removed when warmer weather arrived. [[49]] Even though her friends teased her about her awkward invention attached to a streetcar, Mary didn’t give in to peer pressure. [[50]] By 1913, her invention became standard equipment on American cars. Windshield wipers save lives and make it easier to drive through storms.

options_bank.B: A year later, she received a patent for it.
options_bank.C: Its function of wiping rain was later considered and added.
options_bank.D: Instead, she paid much attention to the streetcar motorman.
options_bank.E: Wiping off the snow and ice by hands, however, seemed to be the only solution.

tags.topic: Mary Anderson’s invention of windshield wipers

sections.title: 五、閱讀測驗(30%)
sections.instructions: 說明：第51至65題，每題請分別根據各篇文章的文意選出最適當的一個選項，標示在答案卡之「選擇題答案區」。每題答對得2分，答錯倒扣2/3分。未答者，不給分亦不扣分。

groups.passage: Both the Eskimos and the Plains Indians used open fires in their shelters for warmth but with very different consequences. The Eskimo house was an airtight igloo made of blocks of ice with a small tunnel-like entrance and a small chimney in the center for smoke from the fire. Temperatures inside this structure easily reached 70 to 80 degrees Fahrenheit although outside temperatures frequently dropped well below zero. Often, the igloo was so hot that the loss of body fluid through perspiration would force the Eskimos to drink cup after cup of ice water. The Plains Indians, on the other hand, placed their fire in a tepee made with long poles and animal skins with an entrance cut directly into one wall. In contrast to the Eskimo shelter, the tepee was far from airtight; drafts came in around the door and through gaps between the skins. At night the Indians would crawl under their blankets, cover their heads, and shiver all night—so much that the blankets would shake! The difference between the Eskimo igloo and the Indian tepee was insulation: the igloo’s walls were solid and airtight whereas those of the tepee permitted a great deal of air to enter.

questions.stem: This passage most likely occurs as part of ______.
From the passage, it can be inferred that ______.

options.A: to enter an Eskimo house, one had to go through a long tunnel
options.B: the Eskimo igloo had better insulation than the Indian tepee
options.C: the Plains Indians enjoyed living in their shelters in winter days
options.D: there was a small chimney in every Indian tepee to release the smoke from the fire

questions.stem: This passage is written mainly to ______.

tags.topic: Eskimo igloos versus Plains Indian tepees: the role of insulation

groups.passage: Soapy’s life was fine during spring, summer and autumn, but not so good in the winter. When November arrived, Soapy always found the way to stay indoors, away from the cold, and had three meals a day without paying one cent. The trick was simple: he broke the law. Last autumn, when nights got too cold to sleep in the park, Soapy realized it was time to make arrangements for his annual winter trip. He walked over to Fifth Avenue around 10 a.m. one morning and sent a stone crashing through a glass window of a big department store. Then he stood calmly by the window, waiting. As he had expected, a policeman came running around the corner. Soapy confessed immediately that he was the one who had broken the window. Yet the policeman did not believe him. Soapy also failed in his second scheme: the woman he tried to harass verbally was, much to his surprise, overwhelmed and in fact thanked him for being the first man ever to say such sweet words to her. It was about noon that Soapy came near a fancy restaurant. He decided to walk in for a big free lunch. When it was time for the bill, he told the manager he had no money and suggested that he have him arrested. The manager, realizing what was going on, asked Soapy to follow him into the kitchen, where a big pile of dirty dishes was waiting to be washed. Three hours later, the exhausted Soapy returned to the street. Then the night came, and it was too cold for Soapy to sleep in Central Park. So he wandered about until he found himself standing in front of a church. The choir were practicing a song. “We often sang it in church. I showed great promise once, but look at me now. I’ve got to change. Yes, I’ll take the job offered last week as a truck driver.” At this moment, the policeman appeared again, arresting him on a charge of vandalism. Soapy was then taken to the night court, where the judge sentenced him to three months in jail.

questions.stem: What is the moral of this story?

options.A: You can do exactly what pleases you.
options.B: One has to pay for what he or she has done.
options.C: It’s never too late to change into a better self.
options.D: We have to get well-prepared for the winters.

questions.stem: Soapy ______.

options.A: broke a big pile of dishes while he was having lunch
options.B: was put in jail though he had decided to turn over a new leaf
options.C: was slapped on the face for saying inappropriate words to a woman
options.D: sang a song with the choir of the church and was greatly moved

questions.stem: Who does he in line 2, paragraph 3 refer to?

refers_to.note: 原卷第三段第2行（題本排版行數）“…and suggested that he have him arrested.” 中以粗斜體印出的 he；同一行另有兩個 he（he told the manager／he had no money）

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about the story is TRUE?

options.A: Soapy usually spent the cold winter in jail where he could have warmth and free meals.
options.B: Though Soapy had a job and a home, he enjoyed wandering on the streets, doing nothing.
options.C: The policeman did not believe what Soapy said because he dressed like a dignified gentleman.
options.D: The judge put Soapy in jail even though Soapy strongly protested that he had done nothing wrong.

tags.topic: Soapy, a homeless man who breaks the law to spend the winter in jail

groups.passage: Queen Victoria was monarch of Great Britain from 1837 until her death in 1901. This period is often called the Victorian Age. Queen Victoria was a stern and serious woman. One reason she was so serious was that she had suffered a great loss. When she was twenty years old, she married a German prince named Albert. Victoria and Albert were deeply in love, and their marriage was extremely happy. In 1861, after they had been married for twenty-one years, Albert died, leaving Queen Victoria heartbroken. For the rest of her life, the lonely Victoria mourned his loss. It was customary in those days for a widow to dress in black for a short time after the death of her husband. But Queen Victoria dressed in black for forty years. And for forty years, as another sign of her grief, she wrote her letters on white paper edged in black. Even before Prince Albert died, Queen Victoria was known as a very serious woman. She had a strong sense of duty and worked very hard at all her tasks. In her diary she wrote, “I love to be employed; I hate to be idle.” She never forgot that she was Britain’s queen and always acted with great dignity. Victoria had high ideals and moral standards that sometimes made her seem stuffy. She was also very sure of herself. She always thought that she was right, and she expected everyone to agree with her.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about Queen Victoria is NOT true according to the passage?

options.A: She had great confidence in herself.
options.B: She ruled Great Britain for sixty-four years.
options.C: She enjoyed her marriage to a German prince.
options.D: She became a serious woman after her beloved husband died.

questions.stem: Queen Victoria wrote her letters on white paper edged in black because ______.

options.A: she was a very stern woman
options.C: that was one way to show her feeling of sadness
options.D: it was a custom among monarchs of Great Britain

questions.stem: All of the following characteristics EXCEPT ______ can be used to properly describe Queen Victoria.
The word mourned here means ______.

refers_to.note: 原卷粗體（選文第二段 the lonely Victoria mourned his loss）

options.A: felt sad or sorrowful in a social situation
options.B: expressed publicly one’s sadness because someone has died
options.C: checked regularly in order to find out what was happening
options.D: included in a group of numbers, ages, measurements with particular fixed limits

tags.topic: Queen Victoria’s grief and serious character

groups.passage:
Boll, a German scientist who was the star of the Manhattan Project, is lecturing at a New York university on the 50th anniversary of the dropping of the atomic bomb on Japan. The speech has become part of his summer routine, self-justifying what was done near the end of World War II. The scientific triumph of his career, in fact, has been paralyzing his life, silently troubling his conscience. He has been haunted with visions of the devastation of the Japanese city, Hiroshima. “Dreams have become nightmares,” he concedes. Then when his wife, an Austrian Jew whose parents were victims of the Nazi death camps, falls seriously ill, she designs a salvation journey for her husband, bringing together Boll and Amai, a woman from Hiroshima who lost her face to the world’s first atomic blast.
Following his speech, Amai, wearing a face reconstructed by the skilled hands of an American surgeon, approaches Boll. Now 56 and a documentary filmmaker, she wants to interview him about his role in making the bomb. Boll looks to Amai to redeem himself for what he has done. And when Amai sees through Boll’s façade to his inner depressed state, she recognizes a shadowy reflection of the despair and exhaustion that possessed the Japanese after the war, and begins to comprehend the price he has paid for victory.

options.A: is a professor at the State University of New York
options.B: has been enjoying the triumph over the Japanese
options.C: was one of the scientists who made atomic bombs
options.D: has convinced himself that he had done nothing wrong

options.A: is a documentary filmmaker, who was not personally involved in World War II
options.B: lost her face in the world’s first atomic bombing and is now wearing a new face
options.C: cannot forgive and forget those who have done so much harm to her and her country
options.D: sees the despair of the bomb-makers and enjoys the price they have paid for what they did

questions.stem: Boll’s wife ______.

options.A: will not forgive the Nazis because her parents were killed in the Nazi concentration camps
options.B: fails to understand how troubled her husband feels after the destruction of Hiroshima
options.C: arranges the meeting for Boll to save him from the recurring nightmares about the atomic bombing
options.D: hopes that Amai will help Boll continue his life career as an atomic bomb-maker after her death

questions.stem: What is the author of the passage trying to tell the readers?

options.A: Killers hardly ever seek forgiveness from their victims.
options.B: People can always justify whatever they have done wrong.
options.C: Boll and his wife take great pride in the success of the Manhattan Project.
options.D: Victory in war will never be gained without paying the price.

tags.topic: an atomic-bomb scientist’s guilt and his meeting with a Hiroshima survivor

sections.title: 英文作文(20%)
sections.instructions:
說明：1. 依提示在「答案卷」上寫一篇英文作文。
2. 文長約120至150個單詞左右。

questions.label: 英文作文
questions.stem: 提示：文章請以“If I won two million dollars in the lottery, I would help …”開始，敘述如果你或妳贏得台灣樂透彩新台幣兩百萬元之後，最想把全數金額拿去幫助的人、機構或組織，並寫出理由。

tags.topic: If I won two million dollars in the lottery, I would help …: the people, institution or organization you would give all the prize money to, and why
using lottery winnings to help others

extraction.method: 本年沒有 Word 版題本。英文部分以 pdftotext -layout 擷取 paper.pdf（Times 字型，文字層正確），選文空格 __n__ 改寫為 [[n]]、跨行與跨頁處接成一段、連續空白壓成單一空白，並以程式把所有選文段落、題幹、選項、選項庫逐一回比 pdftotext 正規化全文（251 段，僅兩句因跨頁頁首而未直接命中，已人工確認相符）；中文部分（大題標題、部分名稱、說明、作文說明與提示）在 PDF 中是 Ghostscript 點陣 Type 3 字型（pdffonts 顯示 A／B 兩個 Type 3 字型、無 ToUnicode），pdftotext 只得到亂碼，改以 pdftoppm 250 dpi 轉圖並以 Read 逐框放大檢視、人工抄錄；以 Read 逐頁檢視題本全部 7 頁影像確認段落、空格位置、斜體／粗體／上標。考試時間取自封面 other.pdf 頁面影像（「考試時間：80 分鐘」）。答案取自 answer.pdf 第 1 頁「九十一學年度指定科目考試國文、英文及數學甲選擇（填）題答案」英文欄（文字層亂碼，以頁面影像逐題抄錄 1–65 題）。統計檔 stats-1.pdf（答對率及鑑別指數表，2 頁）與 stats-2.pdf（選擇題選項分析，6 頁）沒有文字層，以 pdftoppm 200 dpi 轉圖、分段裁切放大後逐格人工抄錄 P、Ph、Pl、Pa–Pe、D、D1–D4 與每題 T／H／L 三列各選項比例；再以程式核對：65 題 stats-2 標「*」選項＝抄錄的官方答案、T 列答案選項比例＝stats-1 的 P、L 列＝Pl、D＝Ph−Pl、D1–D4＝Pa−Pb…Pd−Pe 全部成立，H 列＝Ph 僅 2 題差 1 個百分點（已放大確認為原表差異），T 列含未答加總 99–102%。標註為人工判斷。
issues: 結構核對：與 gsat-spec.json legacy_ast「91」期別完全一致：詞彙與慣用語 1–15（15×1）、綜合測驗 16–30（3篇×5題，15×1）、文意選填 31–40（選項 A–J 共10個，10×1）、篇章結構 41–50（2篇×5空格，各篇選項 A–E 共5個，10×1）、閱讀測驗 51–65（4篇：3＋4＋4＋4題，15×2＝30）、英文作文 20分（文長約120至150個單詞左右）；本年無翻譯題。選擇題 80、非選擇題 20，合計 100。倒扣規則（1/3、1/3、1/9、1/4、2/3）已逐字保留在各大題說明；91 年說明沒有 92 年起的「倒扣到本大題之實得分數為零為止」字句，照題本。考試時間 80 分鐘取自封面 other.pdf。
篇章結構配分：本年篇章結構是 41–50 共 10 題、每題 1 分、答錯倒扣 1/4 分（92 年起改為 5 題×2 分），題本說明為「第41至50題…每題答對得1分，答錯倒扣1/4分」，points 各填 1；兩篇（41–45、46–50）各有自己的選項 A–E，分成 s4g1、s4g2 兩個題組，各自的 options_bank。

中文文字來源：題本中文為點陣 Type 3 字型，文字層無法擷取（gsat-spec 91 期別的 note 亦載明），大題標題、說明、作文說明與提示全部依頁面影像人工抄錄，並逐框放大核對。影像無法分辨「說明：」「提示：」的冒號是「：」(U+FF1A) 還是 92／93 年 Word 版在一、二大題與作文提示用的「︰」(U+FE30)（曾嘗試比對 Type 3 字型的 CharProcs，但 Ghostscript 把字形切成碎片並重新編碼，同一字在不同位置代碼不同，無法據以判斷），一律寫成「：」(U+FF1A)。逗號、句號、引號「」依影像寫成全形，數字、斜線、(A)(J)(E) 與百分比依 pdftotext 抽出的 Times 字元寫成半形。

大題標題與部分名稱：題本為「第壹部份：單一選擇題」「第貳部份：非選擇題」（「部份」照原文），part 填「單一選擇題」「非選擇題」。第三大題在題本排成「三 、 文 意 選 填  (10%)」，括號前的間距比其他大題寬，比照 ast-92／ast-93／gsat-93 寫成「三、文意選填(10%)」。作文大題題本只寫「英文作文(20%)」，沒有「一、」編號，照錄。說明文字在框內的換行是排版，未保留；作文說明的 1.、2. 兩項以換行分開。各題組前的「第16至20題為題組」等標示是版面標題（影像中「為」作「爲」字形），沒有放進 passage。

作文：stem 依 ast-92／ast-93 慣例以「提示：」起首，題本「提示：」單獨一行、說明文字在下一行，合併為一個 stem。提示中的英文句子照題本寫成彎引號與省略號「“If I won two million dollars in the lottery, I would help …”」（help 與 … 之間有空白），引號與前後中文之間不加空白。題本沒有規定段數，tags 不填 paragraphs；給定開頭句的命題式寫作，essay_type 標 topic。本年沒有評分原則檔（units.json 無 scoring），也沒有作文得分分布，作文 answer／accepted_answers／scoring_notes／stats 一律 null，sources.scoring 為空陣列。
題號與 label：作文在題本沒有題號；validator 要求 no 為整數，比照 ast-92／ast-93 等指考檔慣例用 no=1、label「作文」，validator 的「題號重複 [1]」warning 由此而來，屬刻意，label 不重複。
答案：answer.pdf 為 91 指考國文、英文、數學甲合併檔（共 3 頁，文字層亂碼），英文在第 1 頁，以頁面影像逐題抄錄 1–65 題；與 stats-2.pdf 標「*」的標準答案 65 題全部一致（本年 stats-2 在 E–J 欄也有星號，文意選填與篇章結構的答案同樣核對過）。

統計：correct_rate／high_group／low_group／discrimination 取自 stats-1.pdf（P、Ph、Pl、D；報考 113,193、缺考 4,913、到考 108,280 人），option_rates 取自 stats-2.pdf 選項分析 T（全體到考考生）列；兩檔皆無文字層，由頁面影像人工抄錄。文意選填收 A–J 十個選項、篇章結構收 A–E 五個（stats-2 其餘欄皆為 0，未放入），其他題收 A–D。option_rates 不含「未答」(NONE) 欄，因此各題加總為 0.64–0.94（未答比例高的如第64題 36%、第65題 33%、第9、49題 31%、第48、63題 30%；含未答後為 0.99–1.02）。stats-1 另有五等分組 Pa–Pe、D1–D4，stats-2 另有高／低分組各選項比例（H、L 列），schema 無對應欄位未收錄。
統計兩表差異：stats-2 答案選項的 H 列與 stats-1 的 Ph 有 2 處差 1 個百分點——第11題 H 92% vs Ph 91%、第57題 H 78% vs Ph 77%（兩處都已放大影像確認是原表數字，且 stats-1 的 D＝Ph−Pl 以 91、77 計算成立），high_group 一律採 stats-1。

統計特殊值（官方原始數據，已看影像確認）：第8題（perished）P＝0.15、D＝0.19，全體 27% 選 (D) dismissed、25% 未答，多於選正確答案 (A) 的 15%；第19題（where）選 (A) how 的 28% 多於正確答案 (D) 的 26%；第25題 D＝0.19、第52題 D＝0.22 偏低；第8、9、18、52、64題 D4（Pd−Pe）為負值，第64題 D3 亦為 −1。

照原文保留的寫法：第41–45題組「Alice in the Wonderland」（書名通常作 Alice in Wonderland）；第31–40題組「many of them are so[[36]].」題本 so 與空格之間沒有空白、「the world that created them— cyberculture」破折號後有空白，皆照錄；第46–50題組選項 (E)「by hands」、第14題「a shame of the society」、第12題選項「win pride」「take chance」皆照錄。選文與選項的撇號、引號為彎引號（’ “ ”），破折號為 em dash（—）。第62–65題組「Boll’s façade」保留 ç。

格式未保留：第31–40題組 mouse potato、technophobe、Computer、computador、konpyuta、wysiwyg、cyberculture，第41–45題組 Harry Potter、Alice in the Wonderland、You、moon，第58–61題組 forty years、love、hate 為斜體；第62–65題組「50th」的 th 為上標，寫成一般文字；第57題 TRUE、第58題 NOT、第60題 EXCEPT 為粗體。依 schema 一律不保留格式。

第56題「Who does he in line 2, paragraph 3 refer to?」：題本選文第三段第二行有三個 he（he told the manager／he had no money／suggested that he have him arrested），被問的是以粗斜體標出的「suggested that he have him arrested」中的 he（題幹的 he 亦為粗斜體），官方答案 (C) The manager。JSON 不保留粗體與行號版面，純文字下第三段同一句有三個 he 會產生歧義、學生無法作答，因此比照 gsat-110、gsat-112（查證者修正）對「粗體標示的被問代名詞」的做法，在選文中標出被問的那一個（查證者修正時用 ；v1.1 判讀依原卷改為 he，並填 refers_to occurrence=8）；題幹的 he 不加標記。第61題「The word mourned here means」：選文第二段「the lonely Victoria mourned his loss」的 mourned 與題幹的 mourned 為粗體，全文只出現一次；v1.1 判讀在選文以 mourned 標出並填 refers_to。
詞彙題與閱讀題幹的空格照題本一律為 6 個底線（______）。

標註說明（屬判斷）：第2題 take the initiative、第6題 download software 記 collocation；第11–15題四字選項的片語記 phrase／answer_pos phrase；第16題 in fact、第25題 therefore、第29題 however、第31題 In either case、第33題 For one thing、第34題 For example 記 connective；第17題 most of it（回指前句的 fresh water，即不到 3% 的淡水）記 grammar_point pronoun；第18題 may seem numerous but provide just a drop in the bucket 依 but 的對比推知，第30題 an easy arithmetic question 由下一句的反問推知，記 discourse；第19題 Even where… 記 grammar／conjunction／adverb_clause；第22題 Each of… has 記 agreement；第26題 pirated CDs 記 word_form；第28題 devote … to making 記 infinitive_gerund。篇章結構：41 (E) But…、43 (C) But… 記 contrast，42 (D) 為「並非全部虛構」的例子記 example，44 (A) 為前句 all about true things 的補充記 elaboration，45 (B) 與後句 writing history 呼應記 lexical_cohesion，46 (D) Instead、47 (E) however、50 (B) A year later 記 transition_word，48 (A) Her solution was simple. 引出後文裝置說明記 topic_sentence，49 (C) Its 回指 the device 記 pronoun_reference。閱讀：第51題（文章出處）記 inference；第53題 written mainly to 記 purpose；第54題 moral 與第65題作者意旨記 main_idea；比照既有慣例，第57題 TRUE、第58題 NOT true 記 detail，第60題 EXCEPT 記 not_mentioned。題組 sdgs：s2g1 淡水短缺 [6]、s2g2 國際科學奧林匹亞 [4]、s4g2 雨刷發明 [9]、s5g4 原子彈與戰爭的代價 [16]，其餘為空陣列。
